PACK.scope: All source videos, transcript sidecars, slide decks/pages, and confidently mapped historical question-source pages available for Python for computational Problem Solving, Unit_01 (Unit 1: Introduction); missing bucket material is reported as a gap.
PACK.title: UE26CS151A · Unit_01 — Unit 1: Introduction · Complete Unit Master
PACK.subtitle: Source-complete searchable master · transcript, slide text, page visuals and archive references
PACK.compiled_from: Hugging Face PESU_Materials source tree, official units.json catalogue, transcript sidecars, slide text/PDF/PPT sources and the selected First_Year_8enterprise archive; see the provenance datasets in the release ZIP.
PACK.how_to_use: Search this single unit master by lesson, timestamp, slide text or source page. Read the transcript in timestamp order, then compare extracted slide text with its page-faithful source figure. Formula candidates and archive question mappings are explicitly flagged for review.
PACK.pyq_note: Historical question-source excerpts are shown only when a page has a strong text-based unit match. They are source references, not new solutions or exam predictions.
PACK.figure_note: Source figures are full-page renderings of the original slide deck pages. Their exact page text appears separately for search and copying; image-only pages are labelled.
PACK.symbols_remark: No formula candidate is asserted as mathematically verified solely from OCR/transcript text. See datasets/content-index.json for raw candidates and source locators.
PACK.coverage_note: This master retains the source content and provenance for the official unit. It is a DRAFT pending human page-level review; see PACK.gaps and the QA report.
tag_legend: Verbatim or OCR-derived text, kept separate from editorial notes.

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Module

•  In Python, a module is a file that contains code.

•   It can include functions, classes, variables or any runnable code.

•  Basically, a module contains code to perform specific task.

• We can use modules to separate codes in separate files as per their
   functionality.





                                                                                                                                          1

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Advantages of Modules

•  Reusability - makes the code reusable

•  Modularity – Organizing the code into modules logically

•  Separate scopes – separate namespace is defined by the module

•  Grouping - Python modules help us to organize and group the content
  by using files and folders





                                                                                                                                          2

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Need for Modules

•  While working on coding, We need to use many classes, variables,
   functions.

•   If we include everything in a single file, the program may become large.

•  To reduce   size of the code, we can group together some similar
   functions, classes into a collection.

•  That collection is nothing but modules in python.





                                                                                                                                          3

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Packages and Namespace

•  Modules in Python can be grouped together in packages.

•  Packages  organize  the  code  into  logical  groups and  provide  a

  namespace to the modules so that they don’t conflict with modules

   with the same name in other packages.

•  The import statement can also be used to import modules from a

   package, which allows to access the functions and classes defined in the

   package’s modules.



                                                                                                                                          4

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Packages vs. Modules vs. Libraries

•  Modules – contain several functions, variables, classes etc.

•  Packages – contain several modules.

                 - folder that contains various modules as files.

•  Library - a collection of packages and modules used to access built-in

   functionality





                                                                                                                                          5

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Types of Modules

1.  Built-in Modules
    •   Python's standard library comes bundled with a large number of
      modules.
    •  They are called built-in modules.

2.  User-defined Modules
    •  Any file with .py extension and containing Python code is basically
      a module.
    •    It can contain definitions of one or more functions, variables,
       constants ,classes.



                                                                                                                                          6

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


User-defined Modules

•  Any file with .py extension and containing Python code is a module.

•   It can contain definitions of one or more functions, variables, constants

   as well as classes.

•  Any object from a module can be made available to interpreter or

   another Python script by using import statement.





                                                                                                                                          9

Source slide page 12 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms


Creating a Module

•  Crete a file with .py extension

•  Example: Creating a module(module1.py)

   a=10
    print("Welcome to Module-1")
    def f1():
            print("in f1")
    def f2():                                     module1.py
            print("in f2")
    def _f3():
            print("in f3")

                                                                                                                                         10

Source slide page 13 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Import a Module

•  import the functions, and classes defined in a module to another

  module

• When the interpreter encounters an import statement, it imports the

  module if the module is present. Otherwise, ModuleNotFoundError is

   thrown.
•  Syntax - import module_name
       import – the keyword used to import the module
      module_name – name of the module to be imported

•  To access the functions inside the module the dot(.) operator is used.                       11

module1.f2()                                                                usingModule1.py

print("value is", module1.a)

Source slide page 22 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Locating Python Modules
•  Python modules are located by interpreter in following steps.

   ▪   First, it will check for the built-in module.

   ▪    If not built-in module, Search for the Module in the current directory

   ▪    If not found in current directory, Python then searches each directory

        in the shell variable PYTHONPATH (An environment variable, consisting

       of a list of directories).

   ▪    If that also fails python checks the sys.path (A built-in variable within

       the sys module. It contains a installation-dependent list of directories

       configured during Python installation).                                                                20

Sys.path.append()
    •  a built-in function of sys module that can be used with path variable to add a

       import sys

__name__ variable and Modules
•   It is a special variable in Python.

•   If the source file is executed as the main program, the interpreter sets the

  __name__ variable to the value “__main__”.

•   If this file is being imported from another module, __name__ will be set to

   the module’s name.
